correctness.rationale: An exact 400-facet construction gives 65,198 nonempty faces. A fully explicit staged toggle matching has 32,590 pairs; complete topological sorting of all 519,776 nonempty face incidences proves acyclicity. Exactly one zero-cell, sixteen eleven-cells, and one twelve-cell remain. Signed integral gradient elimination yields a single attaching vector with gcd two, and high-dimensional Hurewicz plus a unimodular change of basis proves the 15-sphere plus Moore-space wedge. Independent Alexander-dual field ranks provide a separate consistency check. All computations are reproducible from the supplied standalone code.

originality.rationale: The 2023 and 2024 primary cut-complex papers were inspected for graph families, skeleton criteria, and the triangle-free two-cut theorem. None determines the 5-regular Clebsch ordinary three-cut homotopy type. Published claims for triangle-free edge-disjoint-square graphs do not cover this graph, whose forty four-cycles have four incidences per edge. Indexed searches and comparisons to accessible preceding claims revealed no equivalent or dominating statement. The verified integral Moore summand alongside fifteen free spheres is not implied by known analogous computations for other graphs; unindexed or inaccessible equivalents remain a risk.

value.rationale: The 5-regular Clebsch graph is the unique strongly regular graph on sixteen vertices with parameters (16,5,0,2), with forty overlapping four-cycles. The exact homotopy result reveals a natural high-dimensional two-torsion Moore summand coexisting with fifteen free sphere summands in a graph beyond known torsion-free skeleton and edge-disjoint-square criteria. This is more informative than the rational ranks or a narrow unmotivated numeric table entry, and is likely useful when comparing homotopy behavior of canonical strongly regular graphs and integral cut-complex obstructions to shellability.
